instruction.text: Listen to this excerpt of a play.

atoms.b: Kids, let’s get the house in order for mum. I bet it would make her happy to come home to a clean house after a long day of working at the hospital.
Dad, you know I’m allergic to scented soap. No way am I doing the washing up.
You’re not even allergic, you’re just making that up!
Stop it, Joey. And Rachel, you could just hoover instead, that would help me out a lot.
Ha, bet you thought you could get out of cleaning!
atoms.sound: Hah, bet you thought you could get out of cleaning!

atoms.b: Not so fast, Joey. Let’s make a deal: either you do the washing up or clean the toilet.
Yuck! Fine, I’ll do the washing up.
Wow! Thank you so much! That just made my day.

instruction.text: What helps you identify a drama right away? Fill in the gap in the sentence below.

atoms.b: For the most part, dramas are made up of characters ((++speaking reading)). Unlike in ((++stories newspapers)) where an author can describe something for pages on end, a drama is mostly made up of characters speaking to each other. While information on the scenery and setting is written down for the cast and team, it usually ((++is_not is)) read aloud for the audience. Instead, the audience will see it being performed in the ((++film poem)) or on stage.

instruction.text:
In dramas, the characters have two main ways to speak.
Match the way of speaking to the word.

hint.text:
The prefix 'mono' means 'alone', and 'di' means 'two' or 'double'.
The suffix '-logue' also comes from a Greek word and means 'speech'.

atoms.b: a speech held by a single person
a conversation between at least 2 people
